its alright, The gameplay loop is fun initially and first 2 areas have more effort put into them.
Later on the game gets boring, the story is incredibly average, there is no challenge.
The game is hard carried by the boat upgrading mechanic and when your done with that, your basically done with the game, the story ain't worth it.

consider this a neutral review

If I wrote this after 5 hours it would have been a thumbs up.

After 19 hours I have stopped playing and I'm about 70% through the story but have maxed all categories and it's becoming tedious, not fun to complete.

It had a lot of thought for the intro and you can tell the developers got bored after island #2. 

It's fine, but I wish it was a little less needlessly annoying a little more fun intriguing.

Like you meet 7~ characters in the first few islands then not another unique character for another 3. I'm no longer invested in the story. Just my boat.  Now that it's maxed out I am done.

game seems fine. Its mega fun the first few hours when we explore and getting familiar with the world. At the end its gets epeating but the game story is already at the finishing. About story its fine on the beginning but the cliamax is underwhelming. Maybe due to a lovecraft elements which I'm not familiar with.

Kinda like subnautica but without the base building, music gets repetitive, especially the traveling merchant, and the last 4 hours of the game were extremely grindy and kinda boring but I just wanted to complete the game since I was already invested. Good concept but could have been executed better. Fishing was fun though. The lights upgrades were kinda pointless, honestly if I replayed the game I probably could have beat it in half the time if I prioritized the relics and ignored going for all the upgrades. Only think that really matters is being able to catch fish for relics. Wasted a lot of time not going to each zone in order because yes there really is an order to them. If I only judged this game on the first 4 hours of my 10 hours of gameplay I'd give it a positive review but the end-game is too grindy for me. Wish there were more npcs/progression with characters. Game feels half-baked in some parts
Good setting and story, but the gameplay is too repetitive and does not evolve at all. Quests are very similar and boring. Didn't make it to the end, too boring.

gather round seethers and copers, lest ye miss this schizophrenic wall of text im about to recite to ye

Is this ♥♥♥♥ worth it at 50% off?  Probably not, but you do what you gotta do, get it how you want, but 25$ was too much for what I expected, and never got

Look, I did have fun with this game at first, for maybe 5 hours, while everything was fresh and new, then the monotony set in, the concept is interesting, but it sure as ♥♥♥♥ isn't sunless sea/skies, more like a temu discount lite version
It got to a point where I just watched stuff in the other monitor because it just got uninteresting most of the time, but I was hoping for -something- interesting to happen, like at that point you know you done goofed with your worldbuilding and story

The music needs to be extended, it's the same lazy loops, how hard is it to get a few dudes together and play some real nautica themed songs that last for more than a minute?

Apart from giving you items and ♥♥♥♥, the side quests are basically useless, they're puddle shallow, maybe you get a crumb of lore, that's it, fetch me some fish or smth and thats about it, no point to doing them all unless youre a completionist
Some of the upgrades are plain useless, like why would I need the superfisher9000 when I have the multi-allrounder rod, it's just a research part sink, which you really never get enough of, either you dredge for hours, or you fish grind to buy them

The main story itself was interesting, shallow, and went by like a bullet until it fell flat on its face like [spoiler]oh boy it was all a dream/hallucination ur actually just insane or wtv[/spoiler] its like ok thats cheap and lame, the buildup is to THAT?  Another disappointing ending(s), like you build this whole thing only to do nothing with it, you don't…
Really strong start, but gets boring and tedious fast.

Very great start, nice atmosphere but after 10 hours mark the game feels tedious the main missions where to much from the same thing. 

Tons of people keep saying how the good story is, its more lore than really story and its the atmosphere that is bringing this game to a certain level.

Its worth the buy, but don't expect to play long with it. Overall pleasant experience i really liked the concept. But its small budget i would love to see a more ambitious game with this kind of gameplay in the future. 

Because in the start of the game i was really hooked, the gameplay loop was pretty fun in the beginning.  But once you start with the main quest it becomes tedious very fast, its also just like collecting relics once you have done that the game is allready finished. Still i do agree with all the positive reviews i got my share of fun out of this game

claims.claim: Reviewers praise the game's art style, visual atmosphere, and audio design.

citations.review_text: What a fantastic game. Addicting gameplay loop, fantastic audio, and great atmosphere.

Very enjoyable gameplay loop, definitely somewhat addictive! The visuals are also outstanding (The Pale Beach is particularly gorgeous, and has the best sound design of any region imo) and the writing is compelling. Many interesting characters, but my favorites are the Travelling Merchant and the Airman.
smooth art styles, amazing storyline and word building, incredible ocean diversity and aberration creativity!!! this game is BEAUTIFUL!!!

Short, enjoyable. Progression curve is not super optimal. Everything is hard at the beginning and then you're just swimming in money and you can speedrun the rest of the game.

The ambience, music and design is amazing though! Would recommend
This game can get a little scary sometimes haha, but i really like the vibe and artstyle.
very good and very cool game.  I feel like the pacing as really good and the art and everything is really pretty.  The story gets elaborate and there's lots to explore

"Hey! We made loads of cool art in a seas + lovecraftian setting, want to explore it? Also there's fishing!"
Also the music is perfect! Fits the theme and is always in place. (I'm going to replay the Shadows of Loathing...)

I didn't think fish tetris would end up being such an effective mechanic for a cozy fishing horror game, but I was pleasantly surprised. Making enough room to perfectly fit all of my catches in my cargo and sliding into port at 2am, just under the nose of whatever eldritch horror my madness was manifesting, was an excitement I wasn't expecting from this game. And that's not to mention how pretty this game is, both visually and the soundtrack. Highly recommend!

game seems fine. Its mega fun the first few hours when we explore and getting familiar with the world. At the end its gets epeating but the game story is already at the finishing. About story its fine on the beginning but the cliamax is underwhelming. Maybe due to a lovecraft elements which I'm not familiar with.

No spoilers in this review. I think the game is worth it bought on sale. The DLCs are okay, and Blackstone Key is terrible and doesn't add anything at all.

The inventory sorting, fishing, everything mechanically is very good. Super fun to sort your items, fish, and whatnot! Very creative and exceedingly satisfying. The gameplay is extremely enjoyable. Boating feels like you have to plan it to some extent, which I appreciate. The day-night cycle provides a good balance of winding down and revving up.

They did fetch quests well and they feel rewarding, which is pretty hard to do. The story quests are interesting and fun to do - but there are very few of them. It felt like an "Oh, completing these doesn't transition the game into a second chapter with more?".

The collecting feels like a sidequest, which I'm not a huge fan of. Not a lot of incentive to do since there's little "upgrade" or "reward" for it, in itself. Seeing the weirder fish among them is a reward in itself since they're interesting and their descriptions are fun to read, but not worth the effort to many, I'd think. I wish the descriptions had some more context too but I appreciate them just being horrorly-intriguing.

After you die once, the game loses a sense of stakes to a degree, though it still feels intimidating to encounter the "sinister undercurrent". It's hard to avoid that in horror games sometimes.

The story and ending is a bit flat and makes the game significantly less interesting or scary. You don't find much incentive to continue upgrading your boat or fishing past it, which also sucks. It could've been great with just a little more effort on both fleshing out NPCs and creating incentives, reasons to continue, but it doesn't. Not enough quests, dialogues, notes, and not much to let the player find out plot points instead of outright saying them.

Eldritch horror, and horror in general, benefits from a sense of unknown. The game doesn't really know how to handle that the more you learn.

…

+ fishing and inventory management
+ short, spooky story
+ relaxing
+ great artwork
- ending was just ok

wonderful game! it can get a bit draggy (ha) but the resource managing side of this game is awesome, the landscapes and the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up fish are great, and i loved the foreboding feeling the characters add as the story goes forward, and their personal stories and lives, even through few lines of dialogue. the ending [spoiler]left me a bit disappointed, but [/spoiler] and i felt the dlcs i have tried didn't harmonize extra well with the main game, but overall i would gladly recommend it. (maybe when on sale)

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game features cargo grid space management and inventory tetris mechanics for arranging catches.

citations.review_text:
DREDGE is a single-player fishing adventure with a dark, Lovecraftian undercurrent. The narrative setup skips unnecessary filler: you arrive as a newly hired fisherman who immediately crashes their boat, gets saddled with a debt to the local mayor (cue Animal Crossing deja vu!), and quickly discovers that the surrounding archipelago is consumed by cosmic horror and nightmare creatures of the deep.

[b]The Short Answer: Is It Worth Buying?[/b]
If you want a relaxing yet eerie experience where you can zone out, collect Lovecraftian monstrosities, and admire stylized visuals without overly complex mechanics, then yes, absolutely.

[b]Playtime[/b] 4/10
It takes roughly 9–12 hours to complete the main story campaign, with about 3 additional hours needed to wrap up side quests, secrets, and full encyclopedia entries.

[b]Story[/b] 5/10
You pay off your boat debt while dredging up ancient relics for a mysterious Collector, slowly uncovering the unsettling cosmic secrets plaguing the islands.

[b]Music[/b] 6/10
Moody, atmospheric audio design that shifts seamlessly from calm maritime tunes during the day to tense, nerve-wracking ambiances when fog rolls in at night.

[b]Graphics[/b] 6/10
Striking stylized 3D graphics with excellent atmospheric lighting and uncanny fish designs.

[b]Mechanics[/b] 6/10
The core loop combines simple fishing mini-games with tight cargo-grid space management. Upgrading your vessel unlocks faster engines, specialized rods, and deeper dredging equipment, though the progression mostly offers "more of the same" rather than radically new features.

The insanity and nightmare mechanics are handled brilliantly: staying out after dark fills panic meters, summoning terrifying sea monsters, hallucinations, and phantom rocks that threaten to destroy your hull.

[b]Personal Take[/b]
An incredibly addictive and atmospheric game that strikes a great balance between relaxing fishing and eldritch horror. While the story is kept short and the upgrade tree stays …

pretty close to perfect
the world building, the upgrade and space management mechanics, the fictional biology and mysteries.
if you'd like a lovecraftian open-world breath-of-the-wild out at sea as a fisherman, this might be your game.

I didn't think fish tetris would end up being such an effective mechanic for a cozy fishing horror game, but I was pleasantly surprised. Making enough room to perfectly fit all of my catches in my cargo and sliding into port at 2am, just under the nose of whatever eldritch horror my madness was manifesting, was an excitement I wasn't expecting from this game. And that's not to mention how pretty this game is, both visually and the soundtrack. Highly recommend!

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the gameplay as involving a day-night cycle where daytime offers a peaceful experience while nighttime introduces danger, fear, and tension.

citations.review_text:
What an incredible experience. 🎣🌊 DREDGE takes something as simple as fishing and turns it into an addictive adventure full of mystery, exploration, upgrades, and creepy surprises. Daytime feels peaceful, nighttime feels dangerous, and that contrast is what makes this game so special. Absolute masterpiece for anyone who loves atmospheric games.

I started playing DREDGE thinking it would be a relaxing little fishing game. 🎣

Then the sun went down.

Suddenly I’m driving a tiny boat through pitch-black water, hearing noises I absolutely do NOT want to investigate, while my character is slowly losing his mind. 😂

And what do I do?

“Just one more fish.”

That “one more fish” has cost me my sanity, my sleep schedule, and probably my life.

10/10. Would absolutely ignore the warning signs again. 💀🎣
I don't even like fishing but it's so enjoyable doing it in this game and then trying to rush home before [horrors beyond human comprehension] catch me

Dredge is such a unique experience that is hard to put down. The relaxation of going fishing in the open water mixed with the stress of making sure you can get back to dock before it gets dark is such a real feeling that makes the gameplay loop so great.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe issues with the Mac version where the cursor does not lock properly when moving the camera around.

citations.review_text: This game is calm, exciting, and mysterious. You can also pause it while doing your work at anytime. Although there's an issue where the cursor doesn't lock when you move the camera around using the Mac version. Had to find some workaround for it.

I really, really enjoy this game. I love how subtle the scares are in terms of the story. The big drawback i found was actually a glitch with the ship. 

I upgraded my hull (to the third stage? I think it was the third) and i went to where the tentacle monster was in the Stellar Basin and it killed me, forcing me to reload a prior save. When I did, I still had the upgrade but my ship had been reverted to the rinky-dinky version and i tried a few different ways to reload saves or get my ship to look like it used to with that upgrade but i still only have the smaller ship. Which kinda sucks :( 

Otherwise its a great game and ive found basically nothing else wrong with the gameplay. It would be cool if maybe there was an option added to the shipwright or something to change the look of your ship to prior looks? idk

cohorts.summary: Longer-term players continue to praise the smooth optimization while pointing out frustrating inventory limitations.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the inventory management system as frustrating or irritating, particularly regarding limited cargo space and the lack of an infinite dock inventory.

citations.review_text:
This Thumb up is for the main game, I have also added a DLC section that deserves a profound thumb down, read if you're curious:

MAIN CAMPAIGN: 

This game is for people who are not in a rush.
The Horror is not in what you see, but in what might arrive against your ship from the dark. 
The lovecraftian influences are there, they're just not very scary, they're more like "learn to dodge, learn when madness takes you and act preemptively".

The fishing side is very well made, you can fish up to 230 fishes and variants of same fishes (some lovecraftian mutated fishes), and also you can craft different kind of rods according to the area (Mangrove, Volcanic, Oceanic, etc...). 
Your Bag is not very spacious even after you expand it completely, but it's not that much of a bother in the end. 
 
The power up system is extremely "free" for the player, you can power up your ship to the max from the start and buy what you need from the merchants.  

The initial grinding is even pleasant. 

DLCs:

What I define as total scam are instead the DLCs this game has to offer:

1) The Blackstone Key DLC is a Support Pack, basically the beggar's way in the gaming world to get free money in exchange of a few useless items, which is truly embarassing coming from a Company who sold so much with this game. Avoid. 

2) The Iron Rig DLC adds a new smaller campaign that will give the player additional power ups you don't really need at that point of the game (what use should I have of 20% reeling speed when I'm at end game and all powered up already?) and even forces you to re-upgrade your items from zero in order to fish in specific now-altered areas, basically you will have to grind again to use items you already have but with a substantial improved power-up. How sad could this be? Haha. 

3) The Pale Reach DLC is a very short story probably inspired by At The Mountains Of Madness by Lovecraft, one hour and it's done, you go from point A to B gathering items and unlocking power ups (you gues…

As someone who 100%'d this game, here's my review:
Overall the game is absolute beast, nice lookin' graphics, sound and mechanics, interesting quests and just overall not irritating experience. perfect to play with video on background. although there are some problems for me in this game:
1. interface - this game is almost all about inventory management and the inventory mechanics sometimes can be really-really irritating when you are managing your inventory while fishing.
2. the price is really a bit too high so i'd recommend buying this game when its on sale (especially when deluxe version is on sale)

overall i give this game a strong 8/10!
Guaranteed 10 hrs of fun

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game is well-optimized and runs smoothly on low-end hardware such as potato PCs and the Steam Deck.

citations.review_text: Absolute cinema. Dredge is a little masterpiece where everything in the game is completely perfect. The art design is absolutely beautiful, the music is a total banger, and the story itself is a complete home run. On top of that, it is so incredibly well-optimized that you can play it perfectly on a potato PC without any issues. The world feels alive because the characters are so interesting, and each one comes with their own unique little story to discover. Every single minigame is pure fun, and I had so much genuine enjoyment collecting every single type of fish and creature. Finding the extra unique, creepy "aberrant" versions was incredibly cool and creative. I highly recommend this game to everyone!

Such a well developed game, had so much fun playing it. Perfect steam deck games as well. 
Honestly one of those games you can recommend to anybody.
Great steam deck game, perfect for picking up and playing in short bursts.
